newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech building firms face mixed future - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Czech building firms face mixed future - analysts.

text.p: Czech analysts have forecast mixed prospects for three construction companies traded on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) parallel market, as the country's building boom levels off in some areas but accelerates in others.

Equities analysts polled by Reuters said the largest road and rail builder SSZ a.s. faced a smooth path ahead, but it would be full of risky turns for ZS Brno a.s. and bumpy for housing builder Armabeton a.s..

They said a recent government decision to speed up highway construction by injecting 120 billion crowns through the year 2002 helped SSZ to pursue upgrades of railway corridors throughout the country.
French-based Enterprise Jean Lefebvre holds 59 percent in SSZ, which analysts said helped lead to the company's recovery.
"(SSZ) has recorded a financial recovery since the entry of the French strategic partner, which gives it strength to enter several state tenders at once," said Martin Leskour of Brno Broker Group.
Analysts expect SSZ's net profit to rise to 75-79 million crowns this year from 59 million in 1995. The stock gained 59 crowns on Tuesday to 1,290, and has been labled a buy at these levels.
However, ZS Brno is considered to be a risky investment because of its dependence on state tenders for upgrade contracts on railway corridors.

The firm has sufficient orders for now, and analysts expect net profit to double this year to 40-47 million crowns from 22 million last year with sales rising to 2.5 billion from 2.3 billion. But still they consider the stock risky.
"Due to lack of diversification... and relatively big competition in railway construction, we put (ZS Brno) among more risky companies," said Daniela Kozlova of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.
ZS Brno shares fell 27 crowns on Tuesday to close at 515.

Armabeton, once a heavy industrial construction company which has diversified to apartment building and industrial and commerical property reconstruction, is hindered by a high burden of unpaid receivables, estimated at 300 million crowns.
The firm posted a 37 million crown net profit last year on sales of 2.4 billion, but it said this year's result would drop to red numbers due to provisioning for the unpaid recievables.
"The extent of the loss depends on if there will be only tax-deductable (provisions) created or if all known risks will be covered," said Jiri Susicky of Patria Finance.
Analysts recomended to sell Armabeton stock, which lost 25 crowns to 475 in Tuesday's trading, on a lack of positive signals.
